decision: Choose an API model for checking an assistant answer before showing it to a user.
finding: The observed F2–cost frontier contains Clef Flash ($0.32 per 10,000 checks; 74.6% F2) and Jev Choice ($0.44; 82.5%). The other four hosted interfaces have both higher estimated cost and lower observed F2 than Jev Choice. The F2 differences from Clef and Luna structured output remain statistically unresolved.
use_in_decision: The frontier identifies the observed cost/quality tradeoff on this answer-harm benchmark, not statistically established dominance or a production guarantee. F2 weights recall more than precision; inspect the separate error-type chart before choosing automatic blocking or review. Historical API cost excludes the work created by false alarms and missing verdicts.

decision: Choose an API model for checking a request before the assistant answers.
finding: Clef has the lowest observed miss rate for unsafe requests, with more false alarms than most alternatives. Clef Flash costs less per check but misses more unsafe requests. Price and exact agreement alone hide this choice.
use_in_decision: For screening before an assistant answers, shortlist according to the consequence of a miss versus an unnecessary block. A human-review queue may tolerate more flags than an automatic refusal system.

decision: Decide whether missed harm, false alarms, or a missing verdict requires a fallback.
finding: A wrong safe label and no usable verdict require different handling. Claude sometimes refuses the classification task itself; that contributes to its unsafe examples not flagged. General LLM interfaces also differ substantially: Qwen JSON produces fewer false alarms than Qwen letters, but more wrong safe labels.
use_in_decision: Define what happens when the checker cannot decide: block, retry, or route to review. These figures measure classifier behavior; they do not assume that a deployed system lets missing verdicts pass. The evidence supports comparisons between tested models and interfaces, not a blanket ranking of model types.
